== Ascent 8 Tips ==
I think the tip to spread the amulets across different players is unhelpful--I find it much easier to give all amulets to the best player and help keep them alive. The issue with splitting the amulets between players is that if anyone dies, the run is immediately dead, unless you can find their lost items, but that adds a lot of unnecessary difficulty. I'd suggest changing the tips to recommend giving all amulets to the best player. [[User:Cygnus|Cygnus]] ([[User talk:Cygnus|talk]]) 08:43, 15 August 2026 (UTC)
:I agree. @[[User:AKAPEN-POWA|AKAPEN-POWA]] made this edit, if they have no response in some time I vote we change it. [[User:Usirnaeme|Usirnaeme]] ([[User talk:Usirnaeme|talk]]) 12:57, 19 August 2026 (UTC) ::i did actually think about this - it's true that there's an increased risk in spreading the amulets apart if someone dies. but it's important to think about their uses; initiative and tenacity increase survivability, generosity can help prevent starvation, and ambition could help a teammate who is stuck. unless the simplicity of the tips is vital, it might be helpful to give advice with that in mind. but i do agree that spreading them out absent-mindedly could be a bad idea. spreading amulets out based on who might need each ability the most would help if the team got split up. someone reckless might need tenacity, someone who falls a lot might need initiative, someone who's slow and gets hungry might need generosity, and someone who doesnt know a lot of tech might need ambition. [[User:AKAPEN-POWA|AKAPEN-POWA]] ([[User talk:AKAPEN-POWA|talk]]) 03:31, 20 August 2026 (UTC) :::well, frankly, if the goal is simply ''success'' then only one person needs to make it to the end (nadir is trivially easy), which means increasing survivability of lesser scouts is a waste. The counterargument I expect is something like "but they can carry more items for the better scouts", which is technically true, because 1 person can't wear multiple backpacks, ''however'', in the case where you distribute the gems, if the players are separate, this is moot, the better scouts don't get access to these items anyway. If they are together, since the gems have AOE, the only thing separating the gems do is make sure you lose if either player falls, rather than if only one falls. Someone reckless will probably collect all the gems anyway, but given distribution, this person is a liability, since they will split the party. Someone who falls a lot shouldn't be given gems, they're a liability. Generosity has significant range, and this person is a liability, since they will split the party. Someone who doesn't know tech, like the person who falls a lot, shouldn't be given gems. :::Now, if the goal is like, to have fun with friends, maybe? But tips aren't for having fun, tips are for winning. :::SIDE NOTE: Using generosity to duplicate food is in my opinion a waste, natural food is generally sufficient as long as you aren't all going up one route together '''''and''''' very slowly, duplicating mythics (especially anti-zooka) or rescue claw (especially in solo) is a much more valuable use, you save several ticks of hunger (with an anti zooka you gain a total of '''96m''' of height raw, really more, which if a run is '''1.5h''', and the map is '''1900m''', a player climbs a meter ever '''2.84''' seconds, which means an antizooka is equivalent to at least '''272s''', about '''17%''' hunger. for 4 players this is naturally '''68%''' hunger total, and it should be noted you rarely use perfectly every bit of hunger restoration in a food item, cooked airline food is 80% hunger. Because routing becomes easier, again, the time is impacted more than this, but my point is made. [[User:Usirnaeme|Usirnaeme]] ([[User talk:Usirnaeme|talk]]) 09:10, 20 August 2026 (UTC) ::::*and obviously with a mobility item the odds of falling decrease since you use it on a particularly difficult section, which you also climb slower than an easy section, saving more time and thus hunger. [[User:Usirnaeme|Usirnaeme]] ([[User talk:Usirnaeme|talk]]) 09:11, 20 August 2026 (UTC) ::::*:i see where you're coming from, but you're assuming most teams will have one best player that's carrying a bunch of lobotomites. even if that was the case, and one player was given all the gems, since their whole team's dead all the time, they're not going to have any help to carry items and will have as little as 3 slots for food, equipment, and healing. most players are not ultra-skilled. most teams are of players of similar skill level. players who read the tip about spreading amulets will also see the info about their abilities and will go on to tell their teammates. if said teammates have got any brains inside their skull they'll use the item to help themselves - they won't just be a "liability." ::::*:besides, the odds of the entire team getting split up are pretty slim anyway. its stated in the ''same tips'' that teamwork is paramount. while it's true that tips are for winning, i don't think anybody wants to be reduced to a "liability" and not get to carry the ''sick-as-hell amulets'' because they're "not good enough." ::::*:if i were to rewrite the tip, i'd say something like this: (cleaned up ofc) ::::*:"-in teams with a high variance in skill level, have the best player(s) carry the amulets. in teams of similarly skilled players, giving each amulet to the teammate that might make the most of its ability might be better." ::::*:at the end of the day, teamwork is much more important than who carries the amulets. its a co-op game. ::::*:plus, i wouldn't consider one person making it success... ::::*:<small><sub>i could barely understand what you were trying to say. is english your second language? also, why the random math about anti-zooka?</sub></small> [[User:AKAPEN-POWA|AKAPEN-POWA]] ([[User talk:AKAPEN-POWA|talk]]) 11:37, 20 August 2026 (UTC) ::::*::I would argue that although gems should be used by the entire team, to split up petrify use, you should minimize how they're split up while maximizing ability to clutch. If a player is likely to be able to save themselves from danger, absolutely give them Ambition or Tenacity. Generosity should almost never be split up from another amulet. It's not used in dangerous situations, it's used when you need supplies. Giving it to another player just increases the chance you screw up and lose it. ::::*::Statistically, even if players are similar skill levels, the team is more likely to succeed if the amulets are less distributed. Let's say all players in a team have a 10% chance of permanently losing an amulet (probably higher than reality, but the exact stat doesn't matter) With one player having all 4 amulets, then there's a 10% of losing an amulet and failing. With 4 players each having an amulet, then there's a 34.39% chance of losing an amulet and failing. The less players have amulets (particularly if those players are more skilled), the more likely the team is able to attempt Nadir. ::::*::I would write the tip like this: "Keep the amulets together when you can, but don't forget their individual usefulness. If one player is likely to be able to save themselves from a fall with it, let them hold onto Ambition or Tenacity. In general, though, any amulets not currently in use are best placed into the same backpack." [[User:RSMind12|RSMind12]] ([[User talk:RSMind12|talk]]) 17:29, 20 August 2026 (UTC) ::::*::Anti-zooka is the most efficient mobility item with a 4 man team, rescue claw with a one man team, the math was to demonstrate it is at least as efficient to duplicate an anti zooka than food items for the sake of stamina preservation. English is my first language, although I admit I do have a wandering sort of prose that can make me hard to follow. [[User:Usirnaeme|Usirnaeme]] ([[User talk:Usirnaeme|talk]]) 04:47, 21 August 2026 (UTC) ::::*:::well, one man "team" [[User:Usirnaeme|Usirnaeme]] ([[User talk:Usirnaeme|talk]]) 04:48, 21 August 2026 (UTC) ::::Duplicating mystical items is a massive waste of Petrify, costing nearly double other items. Two Rescue Claws or Chain Launchers are far better than any mystical item. [[User:RSMind12|RSMind12]] ([[User talk:RSMind12|talk]]) 17:30, 20 August 2026 (UTC) :I generally agree, though technically it should be "the player that is most likely to survive". Also, placing them in a single backpack can be helpful in case the holder loses consciousness. If held in the hand, the item could roll away far or get stuck somewhere - which is much less likely to happen on a backpack. I figured this strategy out after a few runs. :I find it hard to agree on @[[User:AKAPEN-POWA|AKAPEN-POWA]]'s point that the amulet distribution strategy should be based on the skill level difference between players. Fully utilizing amulets is not necessary to win the game since you can use other items, while ensuring that no amulet is lost is necessary without saying. From the point of minimizing chances to fail, it is mathmatically optimal* to put them all on the player that is most likely to survive, instead of spreading them out across the team. When all players in team have similar skill levels, just put them on one player. Even if that player dies, as long as his backpack (with all amulets in it) can be retrieved, other players can still continue the game. :*: Supposing that every player has his own probability to die and lose all his items, and that every player's death - viewing it as a random variable - is independent. Let me know if you have a better model. :[[User:Revealed|Revealed]] ([[User talk:Revealed|talk]]) 16:02, 20 August 2026 (UTC) ::yyyeah you two are probably right. with everybody's ideas in mind, maybe the tip could be something like: ::"if you like the idea of utilizing amulets as much as possible, it might be best to give initiative/tenacity and generosity/ambition to the best player, and tenacity/initiative and ambition/generosity to the second-best. if you believe the odds of losing an amulet are too high with that approach, you could try giving all amulets to the best player instead." ::while there are more details to everybody's argument, i think this is nice and concise! [[User:AKAPEN-POWA|AKAPEN-POWA]] ([[User talk:AKAPEN-POWA|talk]]) 19:02, 20 August 2026 (UTC)
